title: Tender offers by vendor shareholders
subject: This guide addresses the circumstances in which ASIC will exercise its discretionary powers to facilitate the sale of shares by tender where at least 20% of a company's shares are being offered for sale. It sets out the procedures required for shareholders seeking to sell their shares in this manner.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Law (now Corporations Act 2001) and is intended for single shareholders or groups of shareholders who believe the value of their shares would be enhanced if sold in a single large parcel. Offering more than 20% of voting shares by tender will contravene certain provisions of the law unless relief is granted by ASIC.
ruling: ASIC will not grant relief unless it is convinced that the tender process has been a serious test of the market, as control of the target company is determined by the auction conducted in the tender process rather than by a public takeover auction. ASIC considers the major enforcement issues in tender offers to be equality of treatment between members of the target company and prevention of a false market in the target company's shares. ASIC will look closely at any attempt by the successful tenderer not to proceed with the subsequent takeover by reliance on a prescribed occurrence, which may constitute unacceptable circumstances. ASIC will strictly enforce section 746(4), as announcement of the successful tenderer constitutes an announcement of an intention to make a takeover bid. ASIC is not obliged to consult third parties before deciding an application under this guide, but recommends that the vendor consent to ASIC consulting the board of the target company.
